change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light/dark values are swapped: post usernames get much fainter in the default light theme
findings.body: `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument when `$primary` is darker than `$secondary`, i.e. for light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51). Before this change the bold username link in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Now the light-theme branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, so on every default light site the poster's name turns light grey. The dark-theme branch also gets the low-contrast value (`$secondary` at 30%) when it should get the mirror of 30%, which is 70%. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the old value as the first argument and mirrors it for `$secondary`. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Swapped arguments change the light-theme color of the flag message length hint
findings.body: The old color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light-theme branch, which `dark-light-choose` returns when `$primary` is darker than `$secondary` (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. So on mobile light themes `.custom-message-length` goes from a faint hint to near-body-text darkness, and dark themes get the inverted value too. The same selector on desktop was converted correctly (desktop/modal.scss:94 uses 70%/30%). Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Topic map h3 on mobile changes from 20% to 50% lightness in light themes
findings.body: The PR describes a dark-theme-only fix, but this line changes the light-theme result too: it was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and the first (light-theme) argument is now 50%. That makes the topic-map headings on mobile noticeably lighter, and as light as the `h4` below them (line 190). The desktop counterpart keeps 20%/80% (desktop/topic-post.scss:321). Unless this is a deliberate redesign, which the PR body doesn't mention, use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Group member name changes from 30% to 50% lightness in light themes
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The light-theme argument is now 50%, so the name is no darker than the `.title` next to it (line 527) and the two lose their visual distinction. This happens on light themes, not only dark ones as the PR claims. The same change was made in mobile/user.scss:497. The mechanical conversion used everywhere else would be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, here and in mobile/user.scss:497.

findings.title: Group member name changes from 30% to 50% lightness in light themes (mobile)
findings.body: Same as desktop/user.scss:522. The old `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became a light-theme value of 50%, the same as `.title` at line 503. This changes light themes, which the PR doesn't describe. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

summary: The PR wraps `scale-color($primary, X)` in `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X), scale-color($secondary, 100-X))`. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument for light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), so done correctly this leaves light themes unchanged. Almost every hunk does it correctly, and embed.css.scss imports the variables file, so the function is defined there. Five lines change light-theme colors, which contradicts the PR's dark-theme-only claim. Two of them have the arguments swapped: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 (post username 30%→70%) and mobile/modal.scss:102 (70%→30%). Three change the lightness value without a stated reason: mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20%→50%), and desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 (30%→50%).
